subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron overflow recovery retain rotated quarantine sidecars only through an explicit Doctor cleanup flow, or should this PR be narrowed to bounded reads/writes without archive rotation?
rationale: The correct lifetime for recovery data is a product and operator-policy choice: automatic deletion risks losing diagnostic data, while indefinite retention leaves disk use unbounded.

options.title: Narrow to bounded I/O
options.body: Remove archive rotation and land only the bounded read/write behavior, leaving any recovery workflow for a separately approved design.

options.title: Doctor-owned cleanup
options.body: Retain rotation but add an explicit Doctor report and operator-invoked cleanup path with tests for archive discovery and deletion.

options.title: Approve bounded retention
options.body: Adopt a documented archive count or age limit only after maintainers explicitly accept deletion of recovery data.

recommendation.title: Narrow to bounded I/O
recommendation.body: Remove archive rotation and land only the bounded read/write behavior, leaving any recovery workflow for a separately approved design.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is a repository-level recovery-data policy decision rather than a mechanical bounded-read change.
